info.title: Agent gRPC API — REST/JSON projection
info.description: REST/JSON projection of the agent gRPC API, served by Envoy `grpc_json_transcoder` (docs/design/rest-openapi/). gRPC is the primary interface; REST is a low-traffic compatibility surface. @generated by `nix run .#gen-openapi` from the .proto (google.api.http) annotations — DO NOT EDIT; the openapi-sync flake check fails on drift.

get.summary:
REST mappings (docs/design/rest-openapi/), under /v1/agent-sessions/. The two
observe RPCs are reads → GET (`session_id` rides as a query param, empty ⇒ the
sole live session): `Subscribe` is server-streaming, so its GET emits a chunked
JSON stream. `Send` DRIVES the agent (arbitrary execution, `--serve-mcp`-class)
→ POST body:*, server-streaming the run.
get.description: Live event stream. The first item is a `status_snapshot`, then the tail.

get.summary: The current session state, one-shot.

post.summary:
Submit a goal and stream the run live (same `SessionEvent` shape as Subscribe,
beginning with a `status_snapshot` and ending on `run_finished`). Dropping the
stream (client disconnect) cancels the in-flight run. `--serve-mcp`-class — see
the header note. UNIMPLEMENTED on an observe-only endpoint (no session driver).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
The goal to run, for `Send`. The driven session's `(user, session)` identity comes
from gRPC metadata (the capacity-attributed tenant key); `session_id` is reserved
for a future explicit-selector path and must be empty in this increment.

get.summary:
REST mappings (docs/design/rest-openapi/), under /v1/embed/. Capabilities and the
single-query EmbedQuery are reads → GET; EmbedDocs carries a repeated CONTENT
payload (document bodies to embed, not a URL-friendly filter), so it is POST
body:* per the content-payload-vs-filter refinement (README convention).
get.description:
The fixed dimensionality and batch ceiling. Fetched so a client can VERIFY
the remote against its configured `[embedder] dimensions` rather than
assuming — a mismatch silently corrupts a vector index.

post.summary:
Exec runs a command to completion (a materially large grant) → POST body:*;
Capabilities is a read → GET. Under /v1/sandbox/.

Under /v1/pty/. `sessions` is the collection — Open (POST) spawns one, List
(GET) / Get (GET /{id}) read, Close (DELETE /{id}) terminates. Write/Resize are
item actions → POST /{id}/…; Read is a cursor read → GET /{id}/read (the cursor
rides as a query param). A pty session id is a path-safe server-minted segment.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Absent ⇒ from the oldest retained byte.

post.summary:
Under /v1/tasks/. The `/v1/tasks` collection carries THREE verbs: POST replaces
the list (Write), GET lists (List), DELETE clears it (Clear — a collection-level
delete with no path param). Update patches one todo matched by its free-text
`content` (not a path-safe id), so — per the convention (no PATCH; content can't
be a path segment) — it is POST `/v1/tasks/update` with the match in the body.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Patches one existing todo, matched by `content`. Absent fields are unchanged.

get.summary:
REST mappings (docs/design/rest-openapi/): reads → GET, deletes → DELETE, every
other mutation/action → POST with `body: "*"`. A prompt's identity is the
(kind, id) pair, so both ride as path params. Paths live under /v1/prompts/.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description:
UNSPECIFIED ⇒ all kinds

 - PROMPT_KIND_SYSTEM: config [agent] system_prompt (override: prompts/system.md)
 - PROMPT_KIND_PREPEND: context.d/prepend/NNNN_*.md
 - PROMPT_KIND_APPEND: context.d/append/NNNN_*.md
 - PROMPT_KIND_MODE_LENS: prompts/lens/<mode>.md (default: compiled lens)
 - PROMPT_KIND_SYSTEM_FRAGMENT: prompts/modes/<mode>/NNNN_*.md — a tagged situational fragment

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
One prompt entry. `builtin` is true when `content` is the compiled/config default
(no operator override file yet). `order` is the numeric `NNNN` filename prefix for
a context.d entry (0 otherwise). `read_only` is reserved (always false today).

get.summary:
The situational fragments selected for a context — the wire form of the loop's
resolver. Returns each selected fragment as a full entry (with its tags), so an
operator sees exactly the set that composes and why. Read-only with a
repeated-scalar filter (`tags`) → GET (each tag rides as a repeated query param).

post.summary:
A preview/assemble read whose request carries a nested message (`context`) +
free-text `goal` → POST `body: "*"` (avoids brittle dotted query expansion; still
side-effect-free).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Preview the assembled context for a goal. `context` (a tag set) selects the
situational fragments folded into the previewed system message — so an operator can
ask "show me the prompt for {mode:review, language:rust}". `mode` is the pre-04
scalar form, honoured as a fallback when `context` is empty (the server derives a
`mode:<mode>` tag from it).

get.summary:
Read / switch the active personality (the head base) live — no restart
(docs/design/prompts/10-portal-selector.md). `Set` re-resolves the base for the
next turn; with `persist` it also writes the new default through ConfigService.

REST mappings (docs/design/rest-openapi/), under /v1/provider/. Capabilities is a
read → GET; both completion paths carry a nested `CompletionRequest` → POST body:*.
`Stream` is the last of the five server-streaming RPCs (the transcoder emits a
chunked JSON stream) — the streaming set is now complete.
get.description: Provider + model capabilities (tool support, context window).

post.summary: Buffered completion.
Streaming completion — one CompletionChunk per increment.
Expand a prompt's `@`-mentions into context blocks, budget-bounded.
post.description:
NOTE the seam's contract, mirrored here: resolution NEVER fails. An
unresolved, denied, or errored reference becomes a warning, so one bad
mention can't fail the turn. `blocked` (over the hard budget) means the
prompt is left unmodified — it is not an error either.

get.summary:
REST mappings (docs/design/rest-openapi/), under /v1/repo/. Object reads are
revision-addressed, and a revision / path is a rev-spec that may contain `/`
(`refs/heads/main`, `dir/file`), so — unlike a `safe_segment` id — it rides as a
query param (GET, unbound fields auto-map to the query string), never a `{param}`
path segment. Lifecycle side-effects → POST `body:"*"`; `WorktreeRemove` → DELETE.

post.summary: toggle without a full Put

Manually queue a review (C8). Opt-in: served only by the full `--serve-fleet`
process (which has an orchestrator); the bare control-plane endpoint returns
UNIMPLEMENTED.

Approve a persisted draft → post it to its forge (C17). Opt-in: served only by the
full `--serve-fleet` process with persisted history wired (the approver needs to
look the draft up + build the row's forge); the bare control plane, or a process
with no history, returns UNIMPLEMENTED. This is the human approval gesture — the
ONLY path that posts; the model's own forge stays read-only (`dry_run`).

List persisted review drafts (C14), newest state per review. Opt-in: served only
by a process with persisted fleet history wired (the `--serve-fleet` process); a
process with no history returns UNIMPLEMENTED. Read-only.

separate `Approve` gesture.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
An operator-defined role card. Mirrors `agent_core::RoleCard`. The permission
shape is a flat, precedence-ordered trio (no oneof): `all` wins; else non-empty

post.description:
NOTE the seam's contract, mirrored here: this RPC reports *detections*, and
an empty result means "nothing found". A backend that cannot run must
return an empty result rather than an error — the `Scanner` trait is
deliberately fail-open on infrastructure failure so an unreachable advisory
database can never block a tool call.

agent.v1.ActivePersonality.description:
The active **personality** — which named base the loop currently runs *as*
(docs/design/prompts/10-portal-selector.md). `id` is one of
`agent_core::ALL_PERSONALITIES` (agent-seddon|pi|hermes|opencode|codex), or `""`
for the default base. The closed set means a hostile id simply fails validation.

agent.v1.ApproveReply.description:
The outcome of an Approve. `status` is one of:
  "posted"         — the draft was posted this call (freshly).
  "already_posted" — idempotent no-op: the draft was already posted.
  "not_found"      — no persisted draft for this `review_id`.
`detail` carries the posted comment/review URL when `status = "posted"`, else "".

agent.v1.AstCallGraph.description:
A subgraph result: nodes, the caller→callee edges among them, and the roots the
query started from.

current.description: The session the caller's own token names.

agent.v1.AuthSessionInfo.description: One auth session. Never carries a token or a refresh handle.

redirectUri.description: Where the IdP sends the browser back; exactly one of `[auth] redirect_uris`.

codeChallenge.description:
The PKCE S256 challenge: base64url (no padding) of SHA-256 of the verifier,
43 characters. The verifier stays with the client until `Exchange`.

authorizeUrl.description: The IdP's authorization URL, with every parameter set; navigate to it.

state.description: Opaque and single use; the IdP echoes it to the redirect URI.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which `state` is no longer accepted.

agent.v1.Branch.description: A branch (or remote-tracking branch) and its resolved head oid.

agent.v1.CallPath.description: One ordered call path (a chain of symbols).

agent.v1.ChangeKind.description: Per-file change class in a base..target diff. MODIFIED is the proto3 zero value.

purpose.description:
What the binding is for: `trigger` (inbound: a PR link there starts a review) |
`progress` (outbound: the C18 announce feed posts lifecycle events there).
A validated string; an absent/unknown value is rejected fail-closed.

agent.v1.ChannelBinding.description: One channel binding: which channel, for which purpose.

agent.v1.ClassifyRequest.description:
The context a classifier judges. The prompt/history are bounded server-side and
never logged verbatim (a hash stands in for the prompt).

agent.v1.CognitionGraph.description:
The document (`agent-core GraphDoc`): flat node map, stable human-chosen
ids, typed edges, zero layout (layout is a GUI-owned sidecar).

fromMode.description:
Mode-aware compaction (adaptive-cognition 02), additive. UNSPECIFIED (the
default for an old client) ⇒ an ordinary budget-triggered compaction. A
switch reshape is requested when `to_mode` is set and differs from `from_mode`.

agent.v1.CompactStats.description:
How a compaction behaved, for the caller's accounting. `action` mirrors
`agent_core::CompactAction`: "budget" | "switch" | "fallback-generic" |
"fallback-drop". A compaction never errors on a dead summarizer — it returns a
fallback result so the caller can see the degradation.

agent.v1.CompletionChunk.description: One increment of a streamed completion (server-streamed by Provider.Stream).

routeHint.description: Routing signals for a routing provider; absent = today's behaviour.

agent.v1.ConfigEdit.description:
One edit: a dotted key-path (e.g. `agent.context`, `pool.members`) and its new
value. A null/absent `value` means delete the key — revert it to the default.

agent.v1.ConfigIssue.description:
One validation finding: the offending path (`""` for a whole-document
finding), a typed `code` (the closed `ConfigIssueCode` set, snake_case), and a
human detail line.

agent.v1.ConfigSchema.description:
A JSON-Schema (draft 2020-12) describing every config field: type, enum
choices, description (from the struct's doc-comments), default, and an
`x-secret` flag on secret fields.

agent.v1.ConfigStatus.description:
Drift between the on-disk file and the running snapshot: `pending` is the set
of leaf paths that differ, `restart_required` is `!pending.is_empty()`.

agent.v1.ConfigValues.description: The effective config (defaults filled) as a JSON object, secrets masked.

agent.v1.ContentBlock.description:
One typed piece of message content (agent-core `ContentBlock`): prose, an
image, or a document. `data` is raw bytes — not base64 — since proto carries
binary natively.

agent.v1.ContextBlock.description: A fixed, user-provided block of context (from a `context.d/` file).

agent.v1.Decision.description:
The policy authorization result. `agent-core::Decision::Allow` maps to
`allowed = true`; `Deny(reason)` maps to `allowed = false` + `deny_reason`.

deleted.description: False when there was no binding with that id.

deleted.title: false when there was no override file to remove (not an error)

packages.title: the import path, empty if unreachable

seq.description: The per-session agreed-response ordinal this digest belongs to.

model.description: The model that produced the distillation (cost/quality attribution).

agent.v1.Digest.description:
One ledger row. `kind` is a CLOSED set ("summary" | "facts" | "objective" |
"alternatives") — an unknown discriminator is rejected/skipped, never stored.

agent.v1.DimensionStep.description: The accepted per-dimension summaries of a step (capped server-side).

agent.v1.DimensionSummary.description:
One dimension's summary of a step. `dimension` is a `safe_segment`'d slug;
`summary` is bounded + injection-screened before it is persisted.

agent.v1.EntryKind.description: The kind of object a TreeEntry points at.

idToken.description: An OIDC ID token (compact JWT) from a configured issuer. At most 16 KiB.

useClientCert.description:
Trade this connection's client certificate for a service token instead of
an ID token (security-hardening S10). Needs a mutual-TLS listener and a
certificate whose URI SAN is in `[auth.mtls] bindings`; `id_token` must be
empty. The token is bound to the certificate (`cnf`), carries
`sub = svc:<name>` and `amr = ["mtls"]`, and has no refresh handle: exchange
again before it expires.

code.description:
A browser sign-in's authorization code (S13), from the IdP's redirect. Needs
`state` and `code_verifier`; `id_token` must be empty. At most 4 KiB.

state.description: The `state` `Begin` returned, echoed by the IdP's redirect. Single use.

codeVerifier.description:
The PKCE verifier whose S256 challenge went to `Begin` (RFC 7636: 43-128
unreserved characters).

accessToken.description: The agent token (compact JWT); send it as `authorization: Bearer <token>`.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which the token is rejected.

principal.description: The identity the token carries (the same fields `WhoAmI` returns).

refreshHandle.description: Opaque; send it to `Refresh` before `expires_at`. Each use returns a new one.

sessionExpiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which the session cannot be refreshed; sign in again.

agent.v1.ExecEnvVar.description:
One per-exec variable set on the child after the env policy is applied, so it
survives EXEC_ENV_POLICY_SCRUB (the campaign worker's owner token). Names must
match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and values must be NUL-free; the backend refuses
the exec before spawning otherwise. Values are treated as secrets.

argv.description: When non-empty, run this argv directly (no shell); `command` is ignored.

stdoutBytes.description:
Exact stdout bytes (`stdout` is a lossy-UTF8 view of this) — preserves a
binary capture (e.g. a git blob object read through the seam).

deleted.title: false when the id was absent (not an error)

id.description:
Identity — path-safe segments (server-validated). The workspace is
`root/<user>/<id>`.

tokenRef.description: Kind-prefixed token reference: `env:NAME` or `file:/path` — NEVER the secret.

skill.description: Review skill/prompt selector ("" ⇒ the default review skill).

slackTriggerChannel.description: Slack triggers ("" ⇒ no Slack trigger / no progress surfacing).

pollSecs.description: Forge poll interval in seconds (clamped to [MIN, MAX] on ingest; 0 ⇒ default).

forgeId.description:
Persisted forge card id (config C36 / D1b). When set, the row's forge is built
from the `ForgeCard` of this id in the `ForgeRegistry` (its kind/base_url/
token_ref/repo_encoding), and the inline `backend`/`base_url`/`token_ref` above
are ignored. Empty ⇒ the inline fields are used (unchanged behavior). Path-safe.

transportId.description:
Persisted transport card id (config C37 / D2b). When set, the row's Slack watch
(and, later, its progress feed) is driven by the `TransportCard` of this id in the
`TransportRegistry`: its `app_token_ref` supplies the Socket-Mode token and its
`trigger`-purpose channel bindings supersede `slack_trigger_channel` above. Empty ⇒
the inline `slack_*` fields + the `[review_fleet.slack]` default token are used
(unchanged behavior). Path-safe.

agent.v1.FleetSession.description:
One durable roster row — a review session's identity, the repo it watches, how
it reaches its forge, and its triggers. Mirrors `agent_core::FleetSession`.

kind.description: Selects the Forge impl factory: github | gitlab | (gitea | bitbucket | …).

enabled.description: Whether this forge is active (a disabled card is stored but not built).

baseUrl.description:
Empty ⇒ the kind's registered default (e.g. https://api.github.com); a non-empty
value overrides it (self-hosted GitLab / GitHub Enterprise) and is SSRF-screened.

repoEncoding.description:
How a flat `owner__name` slug maps to the host API path: `owner_name` (GitHub:
split `owner__name`) | `path` (GitLab: `__`→`/`, subgroups). Required.

maxRetries.description: HTTP retry budget, clamped on ingest.

agent.v1.ForgeCard.description:
A forge (git-host) card. Mirrors `agent_core::ForgeCard`. `kind` selects the impl
factory; `base_url` empty ⇒ the kind's registered default; `repo_encoding` is a
validated scheme string (`owner_name` | `path`).

deleted.title: false when the id was absent (not an error)

comments.description: Populated by ImportIssue; empty in list results.

agent.v1.ForgePrPage.description:
`next_page` absent ⇒ this is the last page, so a caller can paginate without
knowing the platform's pagination dialect.

number.description: The user-facing number (#42), not an internal id.

agent.v1.GoalRequest.description:
The goal to run, for `Send`. The driven session's `(user, session)` identity comes
from gRPC metadata (the capacity-attributed tenant key); `session_id` is reserved
for a future explicit-selector path and must be empty in this increment.

agent.v1.GraphEdge.description: A typed edge. `KIND_UNSPECIFIED` is never valid — conversions reject it.

agent.v1.GraphEdge.Kind.description:
- KIND_MAIN: Data flow on the turn path (acyclic between nodes).
 - KIND_BACKGROUND: Fire-and-forget hand-off to the distiller; only from `anchor.delivery`.
 - KIND_CAPABILITY: Attachment: `from` names a configured resource, `to` the consuming node.

node.description: The offending node id / edge endpoint; "" = a document-level finding.

agent.v1.GraphIssue.description:
One validation finding. `code` is a CLOSED set (see `agent-core
GraphIssueCode`) — an unknown code is rejected at conversion, never stored.

agent.v1.GraphNode.description:
One node instance: a registered type + schema version + parameters
(`agent-core GraphNode`). Schemas are never embedded in documents.

agent.v1.IndexState.description: Freshness of the on-disk index relative to the working tree.

issuers.description: Empty when browser sign-in is not configured (no `[auth] redirect_uris`).

uintValue.title: JSON integers needing the full u64 range

agent.v1.JsonValue.description:
A lossless, fully-binary encoding of an arbitrary JSON value — the wire twin of
agent-core's `serde_json::Value`. Numbers keep their exact type: integers use
the 64-bit `int_value`/`uint_value` arms, non-integers use `double_value`, and
anything beyond native range rides in `big_number` as a decimal string. An unset
`kind` decodes to JSON `null`.

jwksJson.description: The JWK Set document (`{"keys":[...]}`), as served at `/.well-known/jwks.json`.

paths.description: Matching indexed paths, sorted + deduplicated by the backend.

backend.description: The backend that served the response (echoed for attribution).

profile.description: `google` | `entra` | `generic`, so a client can label the button.

revoked.description: False when the session was already revoked or expired.

server.description: Empty ⇒ no server configured for that language.

agent.v1.LspHoverResult.description:
`hover` is absent when the server had nothing to say — distinct from a hover
whose contents are empty.

agent.v1.LspResultMsg.description:
The result is keyed by the method, so the variant is explicit rather than
inferred: a caller that asked for `hover` and received locations should see a
type error, not silently reinterpret them.

agent.v1.LspWorkspaceEdit.description:
Ordered, and a repeated field rather than a map: a rename's edits are applied
per file, and proto3 maps have no defined ordering.

agent.v1.MemoryItem.description: A recalled memory item, ready to inject into context.

content.description:
The message's TEXT, always populated. Kept as field 2 with its original type
so this change stays wire-compatible: a peer built before multimodal landed
still reads the prose of every message, just without the media.

blocks.description:
The full ordered block list. Set only when the content is NOT simply
zero-or-one text block (i.e. when there is media, or several text blocks) —
so the common text-only message costs nothing extra on the wire. When empty,
decoders fold `content` into a single text block.

agent.v1.ModeVerdict.description:
What a classifier saw the incoming work as. `confidence` is untrusted (a pool
vote's self-report) — clamp to 0..=1 on receipt.

supportsVision.description:
Whether the model accepts image content blocks. Carried on the wire so a
`= "grpc"` provider client can strip media BEFORE sending, instead of the
remote model rejecting the whole request.

agent.v1.NodePort.description: A named, nominally-typed port on a node type (editor connection rules).

agent.v1.NodeTypeSchema.description:
Everything an editor needs to render one node type from data alone:
title/doc, typed ports, and a JSON Schema for the params form.

agent.v1.NullValue.description: The sole inhabitant of the JSON `null` type (proto enums need a zero value).

blocks.description:
Typed media the tool produced (a screenshot, an image read off disk).
Additive: `content` remains the text summary every tool populates.

inFlight.description:
Live load + configured weight (GPU pool 01), additive. Both are clamped on
receipt — a remote pool's reported load is untrusted.

maxConcurrency.description: Concurrency cap + current saturation (GPU pool 02), additive.

state.description: Graded liveness + smoothed latency (GPU pool 03), additive.

agent.v1.PoolMemberResult.description:
One member's settled result. `ok=false` carries a class-only `error` (never a
raw body) and no `response`; the batch never fails.

agent.v1.PoolMemberState.description: Graded liveness of a member (GPU pool 03).

agent.v1.PoolTier.description:
Pool member weight class. Mirrors `agent_core::PoolTier`. Moved here from
llm_pool.proto (same package, wire/JSON-identical) so `RouteHint` can carry a
tier floor without an import cycle.

agent.v1.PreflightProbe.description:
One probe's outcome. `status` is "ok" | "warn" | "fail" | "skipped". `detail` is a
status class or a trusted config value (an address/path) — NEVER a resolved secret
or a raw error body. `latency_ms` is the probe's wall-clock.

agent.v1.PreflightReply.description:
The aggregate report. `ok` is the gate: true iff no probe failed (warn/skipped do
not fail). `probes` preserves the probe order.

agent.v1.PreviewRequest.description:
Preview the assembled context for a goal. `context` (a tag set) selects the
situational fragments folded into the previewed system message — so an operator can
ask "show me the prompt for {mode:review, language:rust}". `mode` is the pre-04
scalar form, honoured as a fallback when `context` is empty (the server derives a
`mode:<mode>` tag from it).

error.title: class-only on failure; `series` is empty then

value.title: may be NaN / +-Inf, as Prometheus emits them

agent.v1.PromptContext.description:
The situation a system fragment is selected for: an opaque, bounded tag set (e.g.
mode:review, language:rust). A fragment is selected when its tags are a subset of
this context (docs/design/prompts/04-selection.md). Tags are string-compared only —
never a path segment or SQL — so a hostile value simply matches nothing.

agent.v1.PromptEntry.description:
One prompt entry. `builtin` is true when `content` is the compiled/config default
(no operator override file yet). `order` is the numeric `NNNN` filename prefix for
a context.d entry (0 otherwise). `read_only` is reserved (always false today).

agent.v1.PromptKind.description:
Where a prompt lives. UNSPECIFIED in a List request means "every kind".

 - PROMPT_KIND_SYSTEM: config [agent] system_prompt (override: prompts/system.md)
 - PROMPT_KIND_PREPEND: context.d/prepend/NNNN_*.md
 - PROMPT_KIND_APPEND: context.d/append/NNNN_*.md
 - PROMPT_KIND_MODE_LENS: prompts/lens/<mode>.md (default: compiled lens)
 - PROMPT_KIND_SYSTEM_FRAGMENT: prompts/modes/<mode>/NNNN_*.md — a tagged situational fragment

closed.description: False when there was no such session — not an error.

env.description:
Environment policy for the child (`Scrub` drops host secrets, keeping a
minimal PATH + TERM). Reuses the exec seam's enum.

dropped.description:
Bytes the rolling buffer had already dropped — surfaced rather than
silently omitted, so a caller knows it lost data.

running.description: Running / Closed carry no code; Exited does.

keepSessions.description:
By default a change that takes roles away (replacing a binding with fewer
roles, another subject, or an earlier expiry) revokes the sessions of every
subject the old binding named, so the change applies now rather than at their
next refresh. Set to leave them signed in.

agent.v1.PutConfigResponse.description: Non-empty `issues` means the patch was rejected and **nothing was written**.

warnings.description: Unresolved / denied / injection-blocked / over-budget, for the operator.

blocked.description:
Expansion was refused wholesale (over the hard budget); the caller must
leave the prompt unmodified.

refreshHandle.description: The handle from the last `Exchange` or `Refresh`. At most 1 KiB.

agent.v1.ReindexProgress.description: One increment of reindex progress (server-streamed by SearchService.Reindex).

agent.v1.ReviewAnalysisDigest.description:
The unified analysis digest (review-analysis-depth Stage 2): every
ReviewAnalysisReport's findings deduped, risk-ranked, and rule-bucketed into
one section. Tool-derived — no model.

agent.v1.ReviewAnalysisFinding.description:
One static-analysis finding (a linter diagnostic). All fields are
tool-derived and untrusted: `file` is repo-relative + confined, `message`
bounded. `in_change` marks a finding on a file the change touched.

agent.v1.ReviewAnalyzerRun.description:
The outcome of one linter invocation (`status`: ok | skipped | timeout |
failed). Distinct from a finding — a clean or unrun tool still gets a run.

agent.v1.ReviewCallGraphNode.description:
One function/method node in the call graph. Tool-derived + untrusted: `file`
is repo-relative + confined, strings bounded.

patch.description: Unified-diff hunks (bounded; empty for binary/omitted files). Untrusted.

shellcheck.description: review-fleet C12 collectors — all shaped as ReviewAnalysisReport.

digestSummary.description: Cheap local-LLM prose summary of the digest (Stage 3) — SOFT, may be empty.

agent.v1.ReviewFleetService.ApproveBody.description:
Approve a persisted review draft and post it to its forge (review-fleet C17, the
approve→post tail). `review_id` names the draft row (server-minted Uuid, persisted at
`drafted`); the approval gesture is the ONLY thing that posts — nothing is posted
without an explicit Approve call. Idempotent: a draft already `posted` is a no-op.

agent.v1.ReviewFleetService.ReviewNowBod.description:
Manually queue a review for one roster session's PR (review-fleet C8). Until the
real triggers land (forge poll C6 / Slack watch C7, increment 4), this is how a
review is kicked off. `session_id` names the roster row; `pr_number` the PR to
review.

agent.v1.ReviewFleetService.UpdateReview.description:
Rewrite a draft's markdown body in place (review-fleet C14, the portal's GitHub-style edit).
`review_id` is untrusted wire input, looked up as a bound query arg; the new `body` is written
to the draft's own server-minted `draft_path` (confined under the fleet root, size-capped) —
never a wire-supplied path. Only an un-posted draft is editable: a draft whose status is
`posted` or `approved` is locked (an edit would diverge from what was posted).

agent.v1.ReviewFunctionSummary.description: One cheap-LLM summary of a changed function — SOFT (model-generated), bounded.

agent.v1.ReviewNamingFacts.description: Naming-convention verdicts (case-style strings, not identifier lists).

accepted.title: false ⇒ coalesced into an existing pending/in-flight review

agent.v1.ReviewNowReply.description:
Whether the trigger was queued or folded into one already pending/in-flight (the
bounded queue coalesces duplicates and on overflow — never a silent drop).

agent.v1.ReviewRuleCount.description:
One (tool, rule) tally in the analysis digest — the bucketed summary so a
high-volume rule stays visible past the verbatim finding cap.

agent.v1.ReviewSignatureChange.description:
One changed top-level function signature (the cheap AST subset). Tool-derived
and untrusted: `file` is repo-relative + confined, `before`/`after` bounded.

agent.v1.ReviewStyleFacts.description:
A deterministic house-style fingerprint — distributions/ratios only, no source
or identifiers. `files_scanned == 0` ⇒ the collector did not run.

requestedBy.description:
Who asked for this review (security-hardening S19): `tenant/subject` of each
ReviewNow caller, at most 8; empty when the forge poller or Slack watcher started it.

approvedBy.description:
Who approved the post (`tenant/subject`); empty until posted, or on a server
without auth.

agent.v1.ReviewSummary.description:
One persisted review draft's METADATA (review-fleet C14). Mirrors the non-body
fields of `agent_core::ReviewDraftRecord` — the `.md` body is fetched separately
via `GetReview` (it is large + LLM-authored, so it is never bundled into a list).
`repo` is the roster repo key (`owner__name`); `status` is one of drafted |
approved | posted | superseded.

revoked.description: False when there was no live session with that id.

agent.v1.Role.description:
Conversation role. `ROLE_UNSPECIFIED` is the proto3 zero value and is never a
valid agent-core `Role`; conversions reject it.

id.description: Path-safe id, unique in the tenant.

tenant.description:
Empty on write ⇒ the caller's own tenant. Another tenant needs a host-global
role.

subjectKind.description:
`sub` (subject `<issuer>/<sub>`), `email` (a verified address), `domain`
(every verified address in it) or `mtls_san` (a service peer).

roles.description: Role names; each must exist when the binding is written.

grantedBy.description: Set by the server: who wrote the binding, and when (Unix seconds).

agent.v1.RoleBinding.description:
Grants roles to a subject in one tenant. Roles are resolved when a token is
minted (sign-in and every refresh): the union of the tenant's bindings that
name the caller.

id.description: Path-safe role name (server-validated; may not reuse a built-in id).

crossesTenants.description: Host-global role — may act in any tenant (like the built-in `operator`).

all.description: Every action on every resource type (an admin role). Takes precedence.

actionsOnAll.description:
Actions granted on EVERY resource type (used when `all` is false and `pairs`
is empty). An empty list here (with all=false, no pairs) grants nothing.

pairs.description: Explicit grants (used when `all` is false and this list is non-empty).

agent.v1.RoleCard.description:
An operator-defined role card. Mirrors `agent_core::RoleCard`. The permission
shape is a flat, precedence-ordered trio (no oneof): `all` wins; else non-empty
`pairs`; else `actions_on_all` (possibly empty ⇒ grants nothing).

deleted.title: false when the id was absent (not an error)

agent.v1.RolePermission.description:
One `(action, resource_type)` grant — both validated strings (e.g.
`("write", "registry")`, `("approve", "fleet")`).

agent.v1.RouteDecision.description: What the router would pick for a hint, and why — pure introspection.

agent.v1.RouteHint.description:
Per-request routing signals (model-router 02b). Mirrors
`agent_core::RouteHint`; advisory and fail-soft — the receiver sanitizes every
value (hostile numbers dropped/clamped, over-long override ids dropped) and a
hint can only narrow selection over the receiver's configured fleet.

agent.v1.RouteMatch.description:
The `match` half of a rule: present conditions must all hold. Mirrors the
`[[route.rules]] match` TOML (02); typed enums here, so a typo'd role/mode is
impossible at this layer rather than a startup error.

agent.v1.RoutePolicy.description:
The declarative routing policy: ordered rules + the default preference, plus
the router-wide breaker settings (0 ⇒ the built-in default).

upstreams.title: explicit id order, ahead of the unlisted

policy.description:
Live-signal ordering policy: "" | "cost" | "latency" | "least-loaded".
Validated on ingest; consumed by the registry-backed router (increment 04).

agent.v1.RoutePrefer.description: The `prefer` half: how to order the survivors once a rule matches.

agent.v1.RouteRole.description:
The internal call-site a request originates from. Mirrors
`agent_core::RouteRole` (model-router 02b); UNSPECIFIED ⇒ `None` (the routing
provider applies its own default).

agent.v1.ScanFinding.description:
One finding: which rule fired, how bad, and where.

The matched bytes are deliberately NOT carried — only the span. A denial
reason that echoed them would hand an attacker an oracle for probing what is
gated (parity spec 08). The span is a byte range into the scanned content.

cancelled.description: False when no such job existed — not an error.

detail.description: Answer or error, truncated for storage.

agent.v1.SchedRunOutcome.description:
- SCHED_RUN_OUTCOME_SKIPPED: The previous run was still going — this fire was deliberately dropped
rather than stacked.

agent.v1.SchedSchedule.description:
Mirrors `agent_core::Schedule`. Carried explicitly rather than re-parsed from
`spec` on the client, so a client needs no copy of the cron parser — and can
therefore never disagree with the server about when a job fires.

spec.description:
The schedule as written, e.g. "every 30m", "cron: 0 6 * * *", "in 45m".
Parsed server-side: the parser is the scheduler's, and a spec it rejects
must be rejected at scheduling time rather than silently never firing.

agent.v1.SearchMode.description:
How the query text is interpreted. `SEARCH_MODE_LITERAL` is the proto3 zero
value and the common mode every backend supports.

backend.description: Which backend to query. Empty ⇒ the server's default backend.
The backend that served the response (echoed for attribution).

episodic.description: The recent episodic window to promote from.

agent.v1.SessionCheckpointMeta.description: One node in the branch tree.

statusSnapshot.description:
The initial snapshot delivered first on Subscribe, so a late joiner is
consistent before the live tail arrives.

agent.v1.SessionModeSwitch.description:
Named `Session`-prefixed: the flat `agent.v1` package already has a `ModeSwitch`
in mode.proto (see the same note in session.proto about global message names).

agent.v1.SessionRegistryService.OpenBody.description:
`user` is advisory until the auth follow-up (07-security.md) — the server MAY
override it from a verified token. `session_id` is **never** client-supplied on Open;
the server mints it (removing client-chosen-id collision/prediction) and returns it,
to be carried in `x-agent-session-id` metadata on every later RPC (01-identity.md).

persist.title: also write [agent] personality via ConfigService (new run default)

agent.v1.SummarizeRequest.description: A recent episodic window to summarize (bounded server-side).

agent.v1.SymbolKind.description:
The kind of a code symbol. `SYMBOL_KIND_UNKNOWN` is the proto3 zero value and the
additive fallback for a kind a peer doesn't recognise.

agent.v1.SymbolList.description:
The shared symbol-list response for the symbol-producing verbs (FindSymbol,
Implementations, InterfaceOf).

agent.v1.SymbolRef.description:
How a query names a target symbol: by stable graph id, or by name + optional
package/receiver. Model-supplied strings are matched, never interpolated.

agent.v1.TaskMode.description:
The coarse task mode. Mirrors `agent_core::TaskMode`. Lives here (not
mode.proto) so `RouteHint` below can carry it without an import cycle —
a same-package move, wire/JSON-identical (`breaking: WIRE_JSON`).

agent.v1.TaskUpdateRequest.description: Patches one existing todo, matched by `content`. Absent fields are unchanged.

agent.v1.ToolCall.description: A single tool invocation requested by the model.

agent.v1.ToolContext.description: Ambient context handed to every tool invocation.

parameters.description: JSON Schema for the arguments object.

parallelSafe.description:
Whether the tool is safe to run concurrently with other tool calls (the
`Tool::parallel_safe` contract). Carried so a *remote* tool's concurrency
contract survives the seam — a non-parallel-safe tool (e.g. `bash`) must not
be run concurrently just because it is behind gRPC. Defaults to true.

agent.v1.ToolSchema.description: A tool's advertised interface (what we hand the model).

kind.description: Selects the MessageTransport impl factory: slack | (matrix | teams | irc | …).

enabled.description: Whether this transport is active (a disabled card is stored but not built).

endpoint.description:
Workspace / homeserver / host. Empty ⇒ the kind's registered default; a non-empty
value is an http(s) URL (self-hosted homeserver) and is SSRF-screened.

appTokenRef.description: Inbound (Socket-Mode) token: `env:NAME` | `file:/path` — NEVER a raw token.

botTokenRef.description: Outbound (post) token: `env:NAME` | `file:/path` — NEVER a raw token.

channels.description: Which channels this transport watches (trigger) / posts to (progress).

rateLimitPerMin.description: Outbound posts per minute, clamped on ingest (`0` ⇒ no limit).

agent.v1.TransportCard.description:
A message-transport card. Mirrors `agent_core::TransportCard`. `kind` selects the
impl factory; `endpoint` empty ⇒ the kind's registered default.

deleted.title: false when the id was absent (not an error)

agent.v1.UpdateReviewReply.description:
The outcome of an UpdateReview. `status` is one of:
  "updated"   — the body was rewritten.
  "not_found" — no persisted draft for this `review_id`.
  "locked"    — the draft is `posted`/`approved` and cannot be edited.

kind.description:
"openai-compat" | "anthropic" | "grpc" | "" (resolve `id` as a registered
provider name, like a `[[route.upstreams]]` entry with no endpoint).

apiKeyRef.description: Kind-prefixed key reference: `env:NAME` or `file:/path` — NEVER the secret.

inputCost.description: Economics / perf. Costs are per-Mtok hints (clamped non-negative on ingest).

agent.v1.Upstream.description:
One routable upstream definition + metadata — the "model card". Mirrors
`agent_core::Upstream`. Persisted by the registry stores; `UpstreamHealth`
(live state) deliberately lives in a separate, never-persisted message.

deleted.title: false when the id was absent (not an error)

agent.v1.UpstreamHealth.description: Live state of one upstream — runtime-only, NEVER persisted by any store.

agent.v1.ValidateGraphResponse.description:
Typed findings; empty = valid. A broken document is a list of issues, not an
RPC error (the editor shows them inline while dragging).

body.description: The raw decoded body, not yet reduced to `format`.

subject.description: `user:<issuer>/<sub>` for a person, `svc:<name>` for a service.

email.description: Empty when the identity provider sent none.

permissions.description:
`action:resource` pairs the roles grant in the caller's own tenant, as of when
the token was issued. Empty with `perms_ref` set when the list is too large to
embed; the roles are authoritative either way.

expiresAt.description: Unix seconds after which the token is rejected.

sid.description: The auth session the token belongs to.

agent.v1.WorkingSet.description: The live message window handed to the model each turn.
